title: Hierarchical kernel metrics and sampled-trace integration for prefill/decode scheduling
creator: Priya Nair
description: Add a lightweight, hierarchical per-kernel telemetry layer that ties NVTX ranges, trace spans, and sampled GPU kernel metrics together so we can understand and optimize prefill vs decode scheduling decisions. The goal is to produce actionable metrics with bounded overhead (<2% p99 latency increase in synthetic CI) and clear attribution down to kernel families (attention, matmul, quantized-kernel variants). We will also add a configurable sampling path for full span payloads to avoid high cardinality in production traces.
acceptance_criteria: NVTX zones emitted from runtime map to top-level trace spans with a stable naming scheme and stream anchors
Per-kernel counters (invocation count, cumulative time, median/95/99 latency) exported to monitoring (Prometheus/OTLP) with labels: kernel_family, kernel_variant, stream_id, prefill_or_decode
Sampling control exists (global rate, per-route overrides) and sampled span export rate is documented; default sampling <= 1% for production routes
Overhead validated: end-to-end 95th/99th token latency increase <= 2% in controlled benchmarks; telemetry CPU/GPU memory overhead documented
Dashboard tiles for prefill vs decode kernel split, hot kernel families, and scheduling wait times are available in Console staging and linked in this ticket
PR with runtime changes merged and feature-flag gated; canary rollout executed to 5% traffic with monitoring alerts configured
implementation_plan: Design stable NVTX/trace naming scheme: use prefix 'rt:' and hierarchical separators — e.g. 'rt:prefill/attention/mha:q8_32' to make aggregation easy

Add a lightweight kernel instrumentation shim that emits: kernel_name fingerprint, kernel_family, variant tag, duration_ms, stream_id. Aggregate per-request in-memory and flush to metrics exporter at request completion or on sampling boundary
Implement stream-anchored NVTX ranges so prefill streams and decode streams can be correlated even when kernels execute on different CUDA streams
Integrate sampled full-trace export path: sampler decides on request start; if sampled, attach full span tree and per-kernel timings; otherwise only emit aggregated metrics
Wire metrics to Prometheus/OTLP via existing telemetry pipeline; expose histogram buckets and summary labels for downstream dashboards
Add runtime config: sampling_rate, per_route_overrides, kernel_family_blacklist, max_span_length. Default gated behind feature flag runtime.hierarchical_kernel_metrics
Create UI dashboard prototypes in Console staging (grafana/trace explorer links) and add alert rules for anomalous kernel regressions
Roll out: dev -> staging canary (10% jobs) -> production canary (5% traffic) -> full rollout. Monitor overhead and rollback if alerts fire
testing_plan: Unit tests for NVTX naming and fingerprinting logic
Integration tests: sample control toggles, per-route overrides validated via e2e harness
Synthetic perf harness: run standardized prefill-heavy and decode-heavy workloads and collect baseline vs feature-on runs
Canary metrics validation: ensure sampled-trace rate matches configured sampling_rate and that aggregated metrics converge to sampled distributions
Chaos test: simulate kernel queue delays and ensure stream anchoring preserves correct attribution across streams
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: high-cardinality metrics due to unique kernel names and stream IDs. Mitigation: fingerprint kernel names and only label metrics with kernel_family/variant; keep stream_id ephemeral only for trace spans not long-term metrics
Risk: telemetry overhead impacts latency. Mitigation: default sampling low, provide feature flag to disable aggregation during emergencies, benchmark targets enforced in CI
Risk: naming incompatibility with existing dashboards. Mitigation: provide migration mapping layer and backward-compatible metric aliases for 3 release cycles
Risk: GPU profiler conflicts (NVIDIA CUPTI/NVTX) in customers' environments. Mitigation: make NVTX emission togglable and document interactions with external profilers
